messages.subject: parallel computing
parts:
Hi everybody,

I have a computer with 24 cores. I currently use the 'orderMarkers' function, and I would like paralellize the job: I have about 50 linkage groups, and I would like orderMarkers to order the markers on different linkage groups in parallel.
I have a cross object (mapbt9) and loaded the libraries 'multicore', 'foreach' and 'doMC'.
However if I run

> foreach(i = 1:24,) %dopar% (mapbt9 <- orderMarkers(mapbt9, chr = i))

I can see it using multiple cores but it does not write the results into my cross object mapbt9.
Does any one know where the problem might be?

Any help or comments will be appreciated,
kind regards from Copenhagen,
Philipp

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] parallel computing
parts:
I think what's happening is that each process is pasting the results back on top of mapbt9, so what you get is the result just for whatever chromosome finished last.

I don't have experience with foreach, so I'd use mclapply in the parallel package. Here's some example code. The key thing is to save the separate results from each chromosome and then paste them back together by just grabbing that chromosome component from thecross$geno. I guess the key thing is to note that mclapply returns a list, each element being the result for a different chromosome.

# use hyper dataset, selected chromosomes
data(hyper)
hyper <- hyper[c(1:3,5:9),]

library(parallel)

# do the ordering of markers, one chromosome at a time
result <- mclapply(chrnames(hyper), orderMarkers, cross=hyper, mc.cores=8)
names(result) <- chrnames(hyper)

# combine the results
hyper.reordered <- hyper
for(i in chrnames(hyper))
hyper.reordered$geno[[i]] <- result[[i]]$geno[[i]]

One weakness is that we're passing the full dataset to each process. In the following I create separate cross objects for each chromosome, containing just that chromosome's data:

hypersub <- vector("list", length(chr))
names(hypersub) <- chr
for(i in chr)
hypersub[[i]] <- hyper[i,]

# need to make a simple function to pass to lapply
f <- function(cross, ...) orderMarkers(cross, chr=chrnames(cross)[1], ...)

# we call mclapply a little differently
result2 <- mclapply(hypersub, f, mc.cores=8)

# We combine the results the same way
hyper.reordered <- hyper
for(i in chr)
hyper.reordered$geno[[i]] <- result[[i]]$geno[[i]]

karl
